checks: Gravity and ground collision settle the player.
The scheduled first aircraft starts outside the battle lane without dropping ordnance there.
Enemy aircraft traverses the arena.
Movement controls move the Rigidbody across the ground.
Running along the ground does not consume a jump at collider seams.
A second jump gains height while airborne.
A third airborne jump is rejected.
Landing restores both jumps.
Nearby digging removes terrain cells and rebuilds collision.
A fired rocket impacts terrain, excavates a crater and releases the rocket slot.
A falling bomb collides and damages the player.
Aimed rockets destroy the scheduled opening aircraft and award score.
Clearing all threats advances the wave.
An ordinary wave advances about 1.6 seconds after its last combat aircraft is gone.
Held fire respects one simultaneous rocket.
The first three waves introduce combat with one, two and three aircraft.
The first forty wave plans spend the original wave budget on aircraft and upgrades.
Cargo opportunities occur every fourth wave.
A normal bomber's countdown stops outside the battle lane.
The stored randomized delay resumes on entering the battle lane.
Successive attacks follow the original randomized countdown range.
Normal bombing can occur away from the player instead of requiring a nearby target.
A surface bomb excavates at most forty percent of the previous circular crater's cells.
One surface bomb makes a shallow, visible crater instead of removing several layers.
Player rockets also excavate a compact crater and preserve deeper terrain.
Six groups of eighteen distributed impacts leave at least seventy-five percent of the soil.
Manual digging can still reshape bombarded terrain after 108 ground impacts.
Six hits at one site deepen the crater gradually while leaving soil above bedrock.
A concentrated crater consumes local digging depth even while more than ninety-five percent of global terrain remains.
Further hits keep excavating the crater rather than reaching an artificial damage cap.
A real falling bomb reaches the shallow-crater excavation path on ground impact.
Walking off an edge retains the first jump during coyote time.
A jump just after leaving an edge rises and preserves the air jump.
The landing-buffer fixture starts with both jumps consumed.
A jump pressed shortly before landing executes on contact.
An expired jump buffer does not cause a delayed automatic jump.
Ground movement climbs a single terrain-cell step without a jump.
Step assistance refuses a rise that would intersect a low ceiling.
A wall inside the barrel sweep receives the impact and releases the rocket slot.
Point-blank firing cannot spawn a rocket beyond a thin wall.
Intact soil shields the body before the same explosion excavates its crater.
A shielded explosion produces visible cover feedback.
A second explosion damages the player after the first blast breaches the cover.
Repeated live explosions rebuild dense craters without a runtime exception.
After repeated excavation, chunk meshes remain valid and obsolete colliders are removed.
A fast bomber crosses the arena faster than the standard aircraft.
A fast bomber releases a three-bomb burst while crossing the player.
A helicopter warns before releasing an aimed rocket.
The helicopter settles into a hovering attack offset.
The warning locks a position and gives the player time to move away.
The helicopter launches a live enemy rocket after the warning.
The enemy rocket flies toward the warned position instead of tracking the dodge.
A supply crate descends and does not grant its upgrade remotely.
Walking to a dropped rocket-slot crate increases simultaneous rocket capacity.
Held fire uses both unlocked slots without exceeding capacity.
A piercing crate unlocks penetration without changing rocket slots.
One piercing rocket destroys two separated aircraft along its path.
Penetration hits an armored aircraft once and excludes it from the second impact blast.
Piercing rockets still stop at terrain instead of passing through walls.
Collected upgrades persist through a reserve-life respawn.
Rocket slots stop at three and a duplicate supply converts to score.
A duplicate piercing supply gives score without stacking penetration.
The fully upgraded launcher uses three slots and rejects a fourth shot.
The live scheduler progresses through all six authored waves and introduces the intended threats.
The opening six waves launch a single optional cargo transport on wave four.
Only shot-down transports drop cargo; clearing a wave grants no automatic crate.
The articulated player model retains the established physical capsule.
The character visual updates its walking pose during real movement.
Overlapping explosions reuse a bounded visual-effects pool.
Smoke, fragments and shockwaves return to the pool after their lifetime.
The layered battlefield backdrop is present after wave progression.
A cargo transport flies across the battlefield without attacking the player.
A living cargo transport does not grant its upgrade or release a crate.
An aimed player rocket shoots down a cargo transport and releases exactly one uncollected crate.
The dropped crate preserves the transport's jump-boots cargo.
Reaching the descending boots crate unlocks repeated air jumps.
Jump boots permit a third jump before landing while ordinary double-jump limits remain separately tested.
Repeated air jumps respect the battle's upper boundary instead of leaving the camera view.
Duplicate jump boots convert to score instead of stacking another effect.
Jump boots persist through a reserve-life respawn.
Collecting EMP immediately knocks down the two hostile aircraft in camera view.
EMP leaves offscreen hostiles, cargo transports and already-falling ordnance intact.
EMP defeats do not generate rescue pilots or a chained life windfall.
Repeated EMP pickups reuse a single pulse effect.
The EMP pulse deactivates after its visual lifetime.
An unshot cargo plane exits the map without releasing free cargo.
A defeated hostile aircraft can release a wounded pilot through the configured drop chance.
A wounded pilot descends by parachute and does not grant a life remotely.
A descending pilot lands on the current terrain collision surface.
Approaching a wounded pilot captures him and grants exactly one life.
A thin soil wall blocks nearby pilot capture and supply pickup.
Removing the blocking wall lets the player collect the nearby pilot and crate.
Rescue lives stop at six and further rescues award score.
An exposed wounded pilot can be lost to an enemy explosion.
Uncollected pilots and supply crates each stay bounded at three.
Pause freezes optional aircraft and descending rewards together with combat.
The live scheduler enters the next wave while an ignored cargo plane, pilots, crates and a regular bomb remain.
Ignored pilots, crates and cargo planes expire without leaving permanent reward objects.
Optional resource objects do not count as hostile aircraft.
A real rocket triggers a falling wreck, scores once, and removes the aircraft from the active wave.
The destroyed aircraft falls before it becomes solid terrain.
Landing leaves four destructible metal cells without scoring again.
The wreck forms a solid step, blocks a blast ray, and remains separate from soil retention.
The soldier steps onto the low wreck without jumping.
The normal digging input removes metal cells.
Blast excavation clears the rest of the wreck and its terrain collision.
Metal cannot be placed in the respawn corridor or around the player's body.
Accumulated wreckage stops at twenty-four cells even with space for more.
Pause freezes the simulation.
Resume restores simulation time.

A reserve life respawns a healthy player.
